The person behind the calendar

More music.
Less searching.

Hi, I’m George Mount, founder of Stringfest Analytics. Jazz Watch is a little project for finding a good live set without searching a dozen schedules.

From Cleveland, with a love of music.

I’m based in Cleveland, home to a wonderful music scene. Jazz Watch brings together free jazz broadcasts from clubs, concert series, and music schools—including our own BOP STOP.

It’s a companion to Classical Watch, my calendar of free conservatory livestreams. Part of the inspiration for the name Stringfest comes from string instruments and classical music. These calendars are another way to share the music.

A small experiment, built with AI.

I built Jazz Watch with help from Codex. It brings together music and a familiar part of my analytics work: turning scattered information into something useful. The goal is a simple, carefully checked calendar you can enjoy.

The venues and musicians make the performances possible. Their official pages provide the schedules and viewing destinations, and they retain the rights to their broadcasts. Jazz Watch is an independent guide.

Enjoying the calendar?

Know someone who uses Excel at work? An introduction to my training at Stringfest Analytics is a lovely way to support projects like this.

Before you tune in

Times are shown in your selected time zone, with the original source time beside each set. The calendar checks official schedules daily and can look up to 45 days ahead. Some venues only announce their next show.

Free registration is clearly labeled. Schedules can change, and saved calendar events do not update automatically. When no end time is supplied, calendar downloads reserve 90 minutes as an estimate.

Read the coverage and methodology or get help watching on your TV.

Privacy

Jazz Watch uses Google Analytics to understand visits, general device and location information, and engagement. Google Analytics may use analytics cookies. Advertising storage, advertising personalization, and Google signals are disabled. We remove query strings and fragments from the page and referrer information sent by our tag, and do not measure search terms or sharing-form text. See how Google uses information from sites using its services.

There are no visitor accounts, embedded video players, or remote fonts. Filters live in the page URL so you can bookmark or share your view. GitHub Pages may retain normal server logs.

Sharing controls open only when you choose them. Copying stays in your browser; email, text, and social services receive the details you choose to share. External sites have their own privacy policies.

Corrections, ideas, or a stream we missed?

Contact George. An official concert or livestream link, date, and free-viewing details help me check a suggestion.
